Interesting! The two gray frames swapped boundaries! Before:
- Frame 1: [[18, 22], [18, 27], [23, 27], [23, 22]] (top frame with yellow)
- Frame 2: [[38, 10], [38, 13], [43, 13], [43, 8], [40, 8], [40, 9], [39, 10]] (bottom frame with green, notched)
After:
- Frame 1: [[38, 10], [38, 13], [43, 13], [43, 8], [40, 8], [40, 9], [39, 10]] (now has the notched shape)
- Frame 2: [[18, 22], [18, 27], [23, 27], [23, 22]] (now has the rectangular shape)
So clicking on the gray frame with the yellow block SWAPPED the boundaries of the two gray frames! The top frame now has the notched boundary, and the bottom frame now has the rectangular boundary.
This is a new mechanic: clicking on a gray frame swaps its boundary shape with the other gray frame.
But wait, the green block is still at [[38, 8], [38, 9], [39, 9], [39, 8]] which is the top-left corner. And the bottom frame now has the rectangular boundary [[18, 22], [18, 27], [23, 27], [23, 22]] which is a 5x6 rectangle at rows 18-23, cols 22-27. But the green block is at rows 38-39, cols 8-9, which is NOT inside that boundary.
Wait, that doesn't make sense. Let me re-read the segmentation. The bottom gray frame now has boundary [[18, 22], [18, 27], [23, 27], [23, 22]] but the green block is at [[38, 8], [38, 9], [39, 9], [39, 8]]. The green block is not inside the frame's boundary anymore!
Actually, I think the frame boundaries are just shape descriptors, not actual containers. The green block is still at the same position on the board, but the gray frame's boundary shape changed.
Hmm, but looking at the image, the gray frame at the bottom still contains the green block. So maybe the boundary is just describing the shape of the gray pixels, not the logical container.
Let me think about this differently. The two gray frames have swapped their boundary shapes. The top frame (with yellow block) now has the notched shape, and the bottom frame (with green block) now has the rectangular shape.
Wait, but the green block is still at the same position. So the bottom frame's boundary changed from notched to rectangular, but the green block is still visible. This means the frame's boundary is just the shape of the gray pixels, not a logical container.
OK so the mechanic is: clicking on a gray frame swaps its shape with the other gray frame. This could be part of the puzzle - maybe the goal is to have both frames in specific shapes.
